name: Paul
note: The apostle (in the traditional view), writing as "a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ" (1:1).

name: Titus
note: Paul's "true child according to a common faith" (1:4), left on Crete to set things in order and appoint elders.

name: The Cretans
note: The people of Crete, described by one of their own as "always liars, evil beasts, and idle gluttons" (1:12); the churches were among them.

name: The opponents
note: Unruly men, "vain talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision," who overthrow whole houses for dishonest gain (1:10-16; 3:9-11).

name: Elders (overseers)
note: Leaders Titus is to appoint in every city, who must be blameless (1:5-9).

name: The Cretan prophet
note: "A prophet of their own" quoted in 1:12; ancient writers named him Epimenides, though the letter does not.

name: Artemas and Tychicus
note: One of whom Paul will send to Titus (3:12); Tychicus appears in Acts 20:4, Ephesians 6:21, and Colossians 4:7.

name: Zenas and Apollos
note: Zenas the lawyer and Apollos, to be sent on their journey (3:13).

name: Jesus Christ our Savior
note: Called "our great God and Savior" (2:13), who gave himself to redeem us (2:14).
